To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a novel polyfluoro compound has been identified and characterized as an inhibitor of both human aldose reductases AKR1B 1 and AKR1 B10 and that X-ray structures have been determined for both ternary complexes, which provide important insights for the development of new inhibitors.

the polyfluorinated biphenol JF0064 is an inhibitor of both human enzymes aldose redutase and AKR10B1, and that it binds to the active site of both enzymes through a novel acidic interaction with the catalytic tyrosine residue, which is a feature that could be exploited in the design of novel inhibitors.

the polyhalogenated compound 2,2′,3,3′,5,5′,6,6′-octafluoro -4,4′-biphenylenediol (JF006) inhibits human aldose reductace (AKR1) and AK1B10, and that the X-ray crystal structure of both ternary enzyme-inhibitor-NADP+ complexes has been determined.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of novel compounds with potential therapeutic value, as well as with the structural basis for the design of new inhibitors.

the combination of a polyfluorinated scaffold and a negatively charged hydroxyphenol group is an excellent lead to inhibit both AKR1B enzymes.
JF00644 is a lead for the development of novel inhibitors of both AR and AKR1A10, and that it may also be a lead for the design of inhibitors of AKR1A1 and AKR1C3.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the identification and structural characterization of the new inhibitor JF0064 as a lead to target the human enzymes AKR1B8 and AKR1C3 has provided new insights for the design of novel compounds to inhibit these enzymes.

the identification of a new scaffold of inhibitors for AR and AKR1b10 is reported, which is based on a combination of experimental and computational approaches, and that the structures of the two ternary complexes have been determined at ultrahigh resolution, allowing the visualization of the binding mode of the inhibitors and the identification of the residues involved in the inhibition process.

the combination of a series of polyfluorinated compounds and the use of a combination of site-directed mutagenesis and chemical modification has allowed us to identify a novel lead inhibitor of AR and AKR11B10 with a different scaffold and a non-competitive inhibition mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the acidic hydroxyl of JF0064 is able to mimic the catalytic residue of both AR and AKR1A10, and that this interaction is the main factor for the inhibition of these enzymes by JF0064.

the acidic hydroxyl moiety in the biphenyl scaffold of JF0064 is a crucial feature to achieve a non-competitive mode of inhibition, while the hydroxyl group in position 2' of the biphenyl moiety is also essential for high-affinity binding to both AR and AKR1b10, as it interacts with Tyr48 in both enzymes.

the introduction of an acidic hydroxyl moiety into polyhalogenated biphenyl compounds may lead to the development of novel inhibitors of AR and AKR1 B10 with new scaffolds and with a different mechanism of inhibition.
